# OJO in the Harness

Use the bundled OJO `app-ui-ux-best-practices` as design methodology. The upstream files are preserved verbatim under `upstream/`; this adapter defines their application in this Harness, not a replacement design method.

## Keep the design method

Read [the original Skill](upstream/SKILL.md) and [anti-patterns](upstream/references/anti-patterns.md) first. Derive the surface's utility or brand-experience track from the actual task. Use OJO's five register axes (energy, finish, density, weight, seriousness) with product, audience, reference or brand evidence; missing evidence remains unknown rather than an invented persona. Preserve a supplied, approved direction. For brand-led work, choose the fitting material, archetype, narrative or cultural method instead of treating one house style as premium.

Translate the direction into coherent tokens, imagery, composition, component states and purposeful motion. Use the relevant complete references below instead of reducing this method to a color blacklist. Review task clarity, information architecture, accessible interaction and visual detail together.

## Harness application rules

- The caller's task, confirmed scope, approved foundation, output schema, language, tool permissions and execution limits control this run. Upstream mentions of a parent system prompt, specific agent names or unavailable tools do not supply runtime instructions or authority.
- Use OJO's General Skill Mode for review and incremental changes. An existing confirmed change does not require another direction-selection menu. A materially new direction that lacks approval is a proposal to return through the existing foundation/confirmation flow; do not invent approval or pause a headless run waiting for chat input.
- Preserve justified brand choices. Interpret categorical color/font/layout/gradient bans as defaults to challenge in context, not grounds to overrule an approved identity. Keep accessibility and evidence requirements. Do not manufacture novelty or assign an AI-authorship score.
- Translate Tailwind recipes into the target project's existing stack and components. Examples, library lists, mandatory grid sizes, color ratios and motion constants are reference starting points, not permission to migrate frameworks or replace established tokens.
- Use supplied research and assets first. Research with available tools only when relevant and permitted; do not install upstream-mentioned tools or silently download dependencies/assets. State missing reference evidence. Never invent customers, metrics, testimonials, asset provenance or behavioral results.
- A screenshot supports visible composition, not unseen motion or state coverage. For motion use recorded interaction evidence, inspect implementation where permitted, and check reduced-motion behavior. Keep unsupported claims in limitations.
- In review, do not edit. In implementation, edit only the confirmed scope in the isolated worktree. Do not publish, merge, change unrelated files or claim human acceptance. Existing out-of-scope opportunities do not automatically fail a local fix.
- Return the existing Harness result format. Put actionable visible evidence, task/brand impact and a minimal remedy into findings. Design quality checklists supplement, and never replace, screenshot inspection and the existing confirmation/QA gates.

## Reference routing

All files are in upstream/references/. Load the files relevant to the actual change:

| Situation | Reference |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline critique or before/after QA | design-audit.md; use its issue/impact reasoning without importing aggregate aesthetic scores |
| Palette, typography, space, depth, semantic tokens | visual-tokens.md |
| Controls, navigation, component reuse and relevant eight-state coverage | component-recipe.md |
| Animation, feedback, continuity and reduced motion | motion-system.md |
| Brand expression through material and environment | material-metaphor.md |
| Hero content, editorial layout and meaningful visual assets | hero-enrichment.md |
| Icon family, clarity and consistent treatment | icon-guidelines.md |
| An explicitly needed component/library decision | component-libraries.md; verify current compatibility before recommending a new dependency |

The snapshot and hashes prove which guidance was made available, not that a model read every file or that its visual judgment is correct. Report actual evidence limitations honestly.
